Question: How does QE differ from interest rate cuts?
Answer: Um, so QE is a buzzword a lot of white dudes who watch a lot of YouTubers explain economics and tend to think Libertarianism makes sense and/or lean right in their politics like to throw around thinking it makes them sound like they know what the fuck they’re talking about. QE does not happen unless conditions demand it and the economy is essentially stagnating (i.e. near zero interest rates and no economic growth). Currently, the economy is on fire, growth is just fine, interest rates are high, so CUTTING them is LIKELY going to be sufficient to stimulate more activity and growth (how much remains to be seen). There is zero need to do any QE at all. None. Nada. So that just needed to be made clear up front. The difference is that QE is when the central bank buys securities and bonds directly on the open market, thus, increasing liquidity in financial markets. Cutting interest rates is the central bank removing or adding reserves to the system at will. In the U.S., the Fed controls the money supply almost entirely. So the supply curve, if you were to graph it out is practically vertical. Interest rates are INVERSELY proportional to PRICE. So when you see bond rates go UP, you know the price went DOWN…and vice versa. Same thing with money supply. Lower rates means higher supply. Interest rate is the “price” of money. QE is seriously like a last resort. The central bank is really getting desperate at that point if they start doing that shit because it means they’re running out of options (generally). This is all very technical and hard. That’s why you need to go to school for it and not listen to blogs and YouTube…or Quora.

Question: What factors contribute to the fluctuation in polling numbers between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump in battleground states?
Answer: I can perfectly explain all polling. Ready? The only people who respond to polls are strongly opinionated and highly motivated to share what they think. That makes their point of view worthless. It’s necessarily flawed/error-laded data. The only responses you will get are on the extremes. These things are typically binary choices or multiple choice responses that they give respondents, which is known as a Likert scale. The responses could be something like “On a scale of 1–5 with 1 being the worst and 5 being the best _________” or a series of choices as responses. And then each of those responses will have a score assigned to it. As the respondent, you don’t know what the score is or what the grade weight will be, but it’s safe to assume the pollsters get paid to develop proprietary polling models that can accurately predict outcomes based on responses, so finding the right scores for answers is…how shall we say…lucrative business. The problem is that it’s really fucking hard because there are just too many variables that you can never build into the model. You have no idea who will lie and when, or why, or under what circumstances. Impossible. What you CAN assume is that almost all responses will be the most extreme, so, if you’re smart, you’ll weight those the least…or at least account for that bias. But virtually all pollsters do not (obviously). Then there’s the issue of sampling size. For a poll to be reliable, you need a large enough sample. Well, how big is big enough? The bigger the better…and it needs to be RANDOM, but if your random sample is 87% white and 13% everything else, you’re not going to get a reliable result, are you? Nope. Random, sure, reliable, no. What about controls? There’s like no way to reliably control the result. You need a control group to compare your sample survey to, but you don’t have one. Read the methodology section of all of these weekly political polls. They basically text or call people on their phones with numbers they farm from political party databases. Online polls and phone calls are hardly reliable sample methods and I guarantee you they’re probably re-using respondents week to week (or every few weeks). That necessarily makes the data worthless. Part of the reason they re-use sample clusters is because guys like me don’t allow political pollsters to get through to them. I know they try (I can see all the calls my white list filtered out that never reached me). All this shit combined gives you the poll numbers you see on TV news and on your phones and it’s all bullshit. The polls showing Trump ahead of Biden in the swing states? Not true. Guaranteed.
